docs.title: ibge-geodata
docs.text: ibge-geodata is a Python package for consuming Brazilian territorial data from IBGE with a workflow oriented around GeoPandas, validated coordinates, and reproducible administrative lookups.

docs.title: What Changed In 2.0
docs.text:
• Unified territorial access

Load country, region, intermediate region, immediate region, state, or municipality layers from the same GeoData API.

  • Merged metadata and geometry

Use metadata for plain tabular data or polygons for a merged GeoDataFrame keyed by id.

  • Reusable point locator

GeoLocator caches boundary layers and returns a structured GeoLocation object for repeated queries.

  • Coordinate utilities

GeoCoords validates latitude and longitude, computes distance and bearing, and converts between WGS-84 and projected CRS values.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install ibge-geodata

Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

docs.title: First Look
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, GeoLocator, Quality
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
print(states.polygons[["id", "nome", "sigla"]].head())

locator = GeoLocator()
point = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292)
location = locator.locate(point)

print(location.state)
print(location.municipality)
print(location.to_dict())

docs.title: Main Concepts
docs.text: Object Description GeoData Entry point for polygon download, metadata retrieval, and direct plotting GeoLocator Point-in-polygon lookup across IBGE administrative layers GeoCoords Validated WGS-84 coordinate object with geodesic and CRS helpers GeoLevel Enumeration of supported territorial levels Quality Resolution strategy for boundary downloads

docs.title: Why Use It
docs.text:
• It removes most of the boilerplate around IBGE mesh and locality endpoints.
  • It keeps geometry and metadata aligned in a predictable tabular shape.
  • It gives you a single coordinate model for validation, distance, bearing, and projection transforms.
  • It makes repeated localisation practical by caching polygon layers inside the locator.

docs.title: 🎯 geodata/core/ — Camada Central
docs.text: Responsável pela lógica principal do negócio geográfico.

docs.title: base.py — GeoDataBase
docs.text:
• Classe principal para interação com dados geográficos
  • Responsabilidades: Orquestração, interfaces públicas
  • Delega para:
  • HTTPClient para operações HTTP e cache
  • CacheManager para caminhos e gerenciamento de cache
  • metadata e polygons como propriedades públicas

docs.title: enums.py — Enumerações
docs.text:
Fonte de verdade para todos os tipos enumerados do pacote:

  • SpatialLevel: Níveis espaciais (COUNTRY, REGION, STATE, MUNICIPALITY, etc.)
  • Metadata: Categorias de metadados correspondentes
  • GeoLevel: Combina SpatialLevel e Metadata
  • Quality: Qualidade dos dados (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH)

docs.title: client.py — HTTPClient
docs.text:
• Encapsula toda a lógica HTTP e de cache
  • Métodos:
  • fetch_polygons(): Busca dados espaciais com cache SQLite (TTL de 86400 s)
  • fetch_metadata(): Busca metadados da API IBGE
  • Dependências: hishel, httpx, geopandas

docs.title: models.py — Tipos de Dados
docs.text:
• TypedDict para respostas da API
  • Facilita type-checking com Pylance / MyPy
  • Documenta as estruturas de dados das APIs IBGE

docs.title: locator.py — GeoLocator
docs.text:
• Localização ponto-em-polígono em múltiplos níveis administrativos IBGE
  • Locator com cache reutilizável

docs.title: cache.py — CacheManager
docs.text:
• Gerenciamento centralizado de cache SQLite
  • Métodos:
  • get_cache_dir(): Retorna o diretório plataforma-específico
    • Windows: AppData\Local\geodata_cache\
    • Linux/macOS: ~/.cache/geodata_cache/
  • get_cache_path(geolevel_value, quality_value): Gera o path do arquivo SQLite
  • clear_cache(geolevel_value?, quality_value?): Limpa cache total ou parcial

docs.title: Importações
docs.text:
Todos os pontos de importação abaixo são suportados:

# Topo-level (recomendado para uso geral)
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality, GeoLocator

# Core — enums
from geodata.core.enums import GeoLevel, Quality, SpatialLevel, Metadata

# Core — classes
from geodata.core.client import HTTPClient
from geodata.core.locator import GeoLocator

# Armazenamento
from geodata.storage import CacheManager

# Utilidades
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords
from geodata.utils.exceptions import GeoDataError, CacheError, APIError
from geodata.utils.constants import URL_SPATIAL, DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL

docs.title: Configuração do Cache
docs.text:
Localização: Plataforma-específica

Plataforma Caminho 🐧 Linux ~/.cache/geodata_cache/ 🍎 macOS ~/.cache/geodata_cache/ 🪟 Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\geodata_cache\

Padrão de nomenclatura: {spatial}_{quality}.sqlite

Exemplo: regiao_maxima.sqlite

TTL padrão: 86400 segundos (1 dia)

Limpeza Manual:

from geodata.storage import CacheManager

# Limpar cache específico
CacheManager.clear_cache("regiao", "maxima")

# Limpar todos os caches de um nível
CacheManager.clear_cache("regiao")

# Limpar tudo
CacheManager.clear_cache()

docs.title: Princípios de Design
docs.text:
1. Separação de Responsabilidades — Cache em storage/, HTTP em client.py, enums em enums.py
  2. Type Safety — TypedDicts em models.py, enums em enums.py, compatível com Pylance/MyPy
  3. Testes Organizados — Unit tests rápidos e offline; integration tests com APIs reais separados
  4. Extensibilidade — Camada storage/ preparada para padrão Repository; utils/ extensível

docs.title: Futuras Melhorias
docs.text:
• storage/repository.py — Padrão Repository para troca entre backends (SQLite, PostgreSQL, etc.)
  • utils/validators.py — Validações de entrada centralizadas e reutilizáveis
  • utils/formatters.py — Conversão entre formatos (GeoJSON, WKT, etc.)
  • cli/ — Interface de linha de comando para gerenciamento de cache e downloads offline

docs.title: Executando Testes
docs.text:
# Testes unitários (rápidos, offline)
poetry run pytest tests/unit/ -v

# Testes de integração (requer conexão com a API IBGE)

# Todos os testes
poetry run pytest tests/ -v

poetry run pytest tests/ --cov=geodata --cov-report=html

git checkout -b feat/my-feature

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: These examples focus on the workflows added or clarified in the current release: merged IBGE layers, reusable localisation, and coordinate transformations.

docs.title: Compare territorial levels
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

for level in [GeoLevel.REGION, GeoLevel.STATE, GeoLevel.MUNICIPALITY]:
    layer = GeoData(level, Quality.LOW)
    print(level.name, len(layer.metadata), len(layer.polygons))

docs.title: Build a state map
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)

ax = states.polygons.plot(
    column="sigla",
    cmap="tab20",
    figsize=(14, 10),
    legend=False,
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=0.4,
)
ax.set_title("Brazilian states", fontsize=16)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

docs.title: Export a layer to GeoPackage
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.MEDIUM)
states.polygons.to_file("states.gpkg", driver="GPKG")

docs.title: Locate multiple cities with one cached locator
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoLocator
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

points = {
    "Brasília": GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292),
    "São Paulo": GeoCoords(lat=-23.5505, lon=-46.6333),
    "Manaus": GeoCoords(lat=-3.1190, lon=-60.0217),
    "Porto Alegre": GeoCoords(lat=-30.0346, lon=-51.2177),
}

locator = GeoLocator()

for city, coords in points.items():
    location = locator.locate(coords)
    print(f"{city}: {location.municipality} / {location.state} / {location.region}")

docs.title: Serialize localisation output
docs.text:
import json
from geodata import GeoLocator
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

locator = GeoLocator()
location = locator.locate(GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292))

payload = json.dumps(location.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False)
print(payload)

docs.title: Calculate distances and bearings between capitals
docs.text:
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

capitals = {
    "Brasília": GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292),
    "Recife": GeoCoords(lat=-8.0539, lon=-34.8811),
    "Porto Alegre": GeoCoords(lat=-30.0346, lon=-51.2177),
    "Belém": GeoCoords(lat=-1.4558, lon=-48.5044),
}

origin = capitals["Brasília"]

for city, coords in capitals.items():
    if city == "Brasília":
        continue
    print(city, round(origin.distance_to(coords), 1), round(origin.bearing_to(coords), 1))

docs.title: Convert between WGS-84 and projected CRS
docs.text:
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

point = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292)
easting, northing = point.to_utm("EPSG:32722")
restored = GeoCoords.from_utm(easting, northing, "EPSG:32722")

print((easting, northing))
print(restored)

docs.title: Create coordinates from external payloads
docs.text:
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

from_tuple = GeoCoords.from_tuple((-15.7801, -47.9292))
from_dict = GeoCoords.from_dict({"lat": -15.7801, "lon": -47.9292})

assert from_tuple == from_dict

docs.title: Downloads are slow. How can I reduce startup time?
docs.text:
Use Quality.LOW whenever you do not need detailed borders. This matters most for municipality and regional layers.

from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

municipalities = GeoData(GeoLevel.MUNICIPALITY, Quality.LOW)

docs.title: GeoLocator returned None for a point that should be inside Brazil
docs.text:
The most common cause is a coarse polygon layer near a border. Retry with Quality.HIGH.

from geodata import GeoLocator, Quality

locator = GeoLocator(quality=Quality.HIGH)
location = locator.locate(coords)

docs.title: Does GeoLocator cache anything?
docs.text: Yes. It loads all required polygon layers during construction and keeps them in memory for later locate() calls. If you need to resolve many points, reuse the same GeoLocator instance.

docs.title: Can I access metadata without downloading the merged polygon layer?
docs.text:
Yes. Use the metadata property.

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
print(states.metadata.head())

docs.title: Can I export the geometry to a local file?
docs.text:
Yes. polygons is a standard GeoPandas GeoDataFrame, so you can use GeoPandas writers directly.

states.polygons.to_file("states.gpkg", driver="GPKG")
states.polygons.to_file("states.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")

docs.title: Can I use coordinates from another CRS?
docs.text:
Yes. Convert them to WGS-84 with GeoCoords.from_utm() when the source CRS is projected.

from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

coords = GeoCoords.from_utm(197055.0, 8254536.0, "EPSG:32722")

docs.title: Can I still work with degree-minute-second coordinates?
docs.text:
Yes, but convert them to decimal degrees before constructing GeoCoords.

def dms_to_dd(degrees, minutes, seconds, direction):
    decimal = degrees + minutes / 60 + seconds / 3600
    return -decimal if direction in ("S", "W") else decimal

docs.title: What happens if the IBGE API is unavailable?
docs.text:
The request layer raises an HTTP exception from requests. Handle it in your application if you need retry or fallback logic.

import requests
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

try:
    states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
    polygons = states.polygons
except requests.HTTPError as exc:
    print(f"IBGE API error: {exc}")

docs.title: IBGE data
docs.text:
The geospatial data returned by this package is obtained from the IBGE Mesh API and the IBGE Localities API.

Use of this data is subject to the terms established by IBGE. See the IBGE portal for more information.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page covers the main workflows introduced in the current API: downloading IBGE layers, working with merged metadata, locating points, and using coordinate helpers.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, GeoLocator, Quality
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

docs.title: 1. Choose A Territorial Level
docs.text:
Every data request starts with a GeoLevel and a Quality.

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
municipalities = GeoData(GeoLevel.MUNICIPALITY, Quality.MEDIUM)
country = GeoData(GeoLevel.COUNTRY, Quality.HIGH)
GeoLevel Meaning COUNTRY Brazil as a single polygon REGION North, Northeast, Central-West, Southeast, South INTERMEDIATE_REGION IBGE intermediate regions IMMEDIATE_REGION IBGE immediate regions STATE Federative units MUNICIPALITY Municipalities Quality Trade-off LOW Fastest download and lowest geometry weight MEDIUM Balanced option for analysis HIGH Highest fidelity, slower and heavier

docs.title: 2. Load Metadata Or Polygons
docs.text:
GeoData exposes two main views over the same IBGE source.

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)

# Tabular metadata only
metadata = states.metadata
print(metadata[["id", "nome", "sigla"]].head())

# Merged metadata plus geometry
polygons = states.polygons
print(polygons[["id", "nome", "sigla", "geometry"]].head())

The polygons property returns a GeoDataFrame already aligned by id, so no extra merge step is needed.

docs.title: 3. Plot Directly
docs.text:
GeoData.plot() forwards keyword arguments to GeoPandas.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

states.plot(
    column="sigla",
    figsize=(11, 8),
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=0.4,
    legend=False,
)
plt.title("Brazilian states")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

docs.title: 4. Validate Coordinates
docs.text:
GeoCoords keeps latitude and longitude in decimal degrees and validates them on construction.

brasilia = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292)
print(brasilia.to_tuple())
print(brasilia.to_dict())
print(brasilia.to_shapely_point())

Alternative constructors are available when your input is not already a pair of named arguments.

GeoCoords.from_tuple((-15.7801, -47.9292))
GeoCoords.from_dict({"lat": -15.7801, "lon": -47.9292})

docs.title: 5. Compute Distance, Bearing, And CRS Transforms
docs.text:
manaus = GeoCoords(lat=-3.1190, lon=-60.0217)

print(round(brasilia.distance_to(manaus), 1))
print(round(brasilia.bearing_to(manaus), 1))

easting, northing = brasilia.to_utm("EPSG:32722")
restored = GeoCoords.from_utm(easting, northing, "EPSG:32722")
print(restored)

docs.title: 6. Locate Administrative Divisions
docs.text:
GeoLocator loads and caches boundary layers once, then reuses them for repeated point lookups.

locator = GeoLocator(quality=Quality.LOW)
location = locator.locate(brasilia)

print(location.municipality)
print(location.state)
print(location.region)
print(location.intermediate_region)
print(location.immediate_region)
print(location.to_dict())

docs.title: 7. Reuse The Same Locator For Batch Queries
docs.text:
locator = GeoLocator()

points = [
    GeoCoords(lat=-23.5505, lon=-46.6333),
    GeoCoords(lat=-30.0346, lon=-51.2177),
    GeoCoords(lat=-1.4558, lon=-48.5044),
]

for point in points:
    print(locator.locate(point).state)

Quality vs speed

Use Quality.LOW for exploratory work and repeated lookups. If a point lies close to a border, retry with Quality.HIGH.

docs.title: GeoCoords
docs.text:
Represents a validated WGS-84 geographic coordinate pair.

from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
GeoCoords(lat: float, lon: float)
Parameter Valid range Description lat [-90, 90] Latitude in decimal degrees lon [-180, 180] Longitude in decimal degrees

Values are coerced to float automatically. Invalid types raise TypeError; out-of-range values raise ValueError.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Type Description lat float Latitude lon float Longitude

docs.title: from_tuple
docs.text:
@staticmethod
def from_tuple(coords: tuple[float, float]) -> GeoCoords

p = GeoCoords.from_tuple((-15.7801, -47.9292))

docs.title: from_dict
docs.text:
@staticmethod
def from_dict(data: dict[str, float]) -> GeoCoords

p = GeoCoords.from_dict({"lat": -15.7801, "lon": -47.9292})

docs.title: from_utm
docs.text:
@staticmethod
def from_utm(easting: float, northing: float, source_crs: str) -> GeoCoords

p = GeoCoords.from_utm(197055.0, 8254536.0, "EPSG:32722")

This method converts projected coordinates to latitude and longitude using pyproj.

docs.title: to_utm
docs.text:
easting, northing = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292).to_utm("EPSG:32722")

target_crs may be any CRS string accepted by pyproj.

docs.title: to_shapely_point
docs.text:
point = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292).to_shapely_point()
# POINT (-47.9292 -15.7801)

docs.title: distance_to
docs.text:
Great-circle distance in km using the Haversine formula.

brasilia = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292)
manaus   = GeoCoords(lat=-3.1190,  lon=-60.0217)

print(brasilia.distance_to(manaus))  # ~2689.6 km

docs.title: bearing_to
docs.text:
Initial bearing in degrees (0–360°), measured clockwise from true north.

print(brasilia.bearing_to(manaus))  # ~322.0°

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Coordinates are always stored internally as decimal degrees in WGS-84.
  • to_shapely_point() returns a Point(lon, lat), which matches GIS axis order.
  • CRS transformers are cached internally to reduce repeated conversion overhead.

docs.title: GeoData
docs.text:
GeoData is the main entry point for loading IBGE territorial meshes and aligned locality metadata.

from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
GeoData(geolevel: GeoLevel, quality: Quality)
Parameter Type Description geolevel GeoLevel Territorial level to fetch quality Quality Polygon resolution requested from the mesh API

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
@property
def metadata(self) -> pd.DataFrame

Returns a plain DataFrame from the IBGE localities endpoint. Columns are normalised so the requested level is exposed with a predictable shape such as id, nome, sigla, and parent administrative fields when available.

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
print(states.metadata[["id", "nome", "sigla"]].head())

docs.title: polygons
docs.text:
@property
def polygons(self) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame

Returns a merged GeoDataFrame containing geometry plus metadata aligned by id.

states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)
gdf = states.polygons
print(gdf.columns)

For GeoLevel.COUNTRY, the result is a single polygon in EPSG:4674.

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
def plot(self, **kwargs) -> None

Convenience wrapper around self.polygons.plot(**kwargs).

states.plot(column="sigla", figsize=(12, 8), edgecolor="white")

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Data is requested lazily when metadata or polygons is accessed.
  • polygons triggers both geometry and metadata retrieval for non-country levels.
  • CRS is preserved from the geometry payload when available, otherwise it falls back to EPSG:4674.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

municipalities = GeoData(GeoLevel.MUNICIPALITY, Quality.MEDIUM)
print(len(municipalities.metadata))
print(municipalities.polygons.head())

docs.title: GeoLevel
docs.text:
Enum representing the geographic level of a territorial division.

from geodata import GeoLevel

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Member spatial metadata Description COUNTRY "paises" "paises" Brazil (country level) REGION "regiao" "regioes" Macro-regions INTERMEDIATE_REGION "regiao-intermediaria" "regioes-intermediarias" Intermediate regions IMMEDIATE_REGION "regiao-imediata" "regioes-imediatas" Immediate regions STATE "UF" "estados" Federative units MUNICIPALITY "municipio" "municipios" Municipalities

docs.title: Member attributes
docs.text:
Each GeoLevel member exposes two sub-attributes used internally:

Attribute Type Usage .spatial SpatialLevel intrarregiao parameter of the mesh API .metadata Metadata URL segment of the localities API

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

geodata = GeoData(GeoLevel.MUNICIPALITY, Quality.LOW)
print(geodata.polygons.head())

Iterate over all levels:

for level in GeoLevel:
    print(level.name, level.spatial)

GeoLevel is also used internally by GeoLocator to iterate through all boundary layers.

docs.title: GeoLocator
docs.text:
Locates the administrative divisions that contain a geographic point.

from geodata import GeoLocator, Quality
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
GeoLocator(quality: Quality = Quality.LOW)
Parameter Type Default Description quality Quality Quality.LOW Resolution of the downloaded polygons

Polygon layers for all administrative levels are loaded and cached on construction, so repeated calls to locate() reuse the same in-memory data.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Type Description quality Quality Polygon resolution used when loading boundary layers

docs.title: locate
docs.text:
def locate(self, coords: GeoCoords) -> GeoLocation

Performs a point-in-polygon test for all administrative levels and returns a GeoLocation with the results.

Parameter Type Description coords GeoCoords Geographic point to locate

Returns: GeoLocation

locator  = GeoLocator()
coords   = GeoCoords(lat=-15.7801, lon=-47.9292)  # Brasília
location = locator.locate(coords)

print(location.municipality)         # 'Brasília'
print(location.state)                # 'Distrito Federal'
print(location.region)               # 'Centro-Oeste'
print(location.intermediate_region)  # 'Brasília'
print(location.immediate_region)     # 'Brasília'

docs.title: GeoLocation
docs.text: Data class returned by GeoLocator.locate().

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description municipality str \| None Municipality name, or None if the point is outside Brazil state str \| None State full name (e.g. 'São Paulo', 'Distrito Federal') region str \| None Macro-region name (e.g. 'Sudeste', 'Centro-Oeste') intermediate_region str \| None Intermediate region name immediate_region str \| None Immediate region name

None is returned for any level where the point falls outside all polygons (e.g. at sea or near a border gap).

docs.title: to_dict
docs.text:
def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str | None]

Serialises the GeoLocation to a plain dictionary.

location.to_dict()
# {
#     "municipality":        "Brasília",
#     "state":               "Distrito Federal",
#     "immediate_region":    "Brasília",
#     "intermediate_region": "Brasília",
#     "region":              "Centro-Oeste",
# }

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoLocator, Quality
from geodata.utils.geocoords import GeoCoords

coords   = GeoCoords(lat=-23.5505, lon=-46.6333)  # São Paulo
locator  = GeoLocator(quality=Quality.LOW)
location = locator.locate(coords)

print(location.state)                # 'São Paulo'
print(location.municipality)         # 'São Paulo'
print(location.region)               # 'Sudeste'
print(location.intermediate_region)
print(location.immediate_region)

# Serialise to dict
print(location.to_dict())

Point near a border

For points very close to state borders, use Quality.HIGH to ensure the low-resolution geometry does not exclude the point.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
Enum that controls the resolution of polygons downloaded from the IBGE mesh API.

from geodata import Quality

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Member API value Description LOW "minima" Lowest resolution — smallest files, fastest download MEDIUM "intermediaria" Intermediate resolution HIGH "maxima" Highest resolution — most accurate boundaries

docs.title: When to use each level
docs.text:
Situation Recommended quality General visualisations / dashboards LOW Regional analyses MEDIUM Points near borders HIGH Cartographic publications HIGH

Higher quality levels improve border fidelity but increase download size and in-memory geometry cost.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from geodata import GeoData, GeoLevel, Quality

# Fast download for exploration
states = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.LOW)

# High-accuracy download for analysis
states_hq = GeoData(GeoLevel.STATE, Quality.HIGH)
